reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational tension in psychological modeling lies between normative and individual approaches. Normative psychology seeks universal laws by testing many stimuli on few subjects, whereas individual psychology tests few stimuli on many subjects. This duality implies a bifurcation in variable space: normative models assume fixed M-variables (gestalts) that map to behavior, while individual models treat these as stochastic parameters varying across subjects. The failure mode occurs when either approach cannot bridge the gap between internal structure (M) and external behavior (R), especially in complex systems where gestalt emergence is not well-defined. In GSI, this manifests as a need for Bayesian hierarchical modeling to infer both population-level and subject-specific behavioral laws. In GSE, it necessitates dual-state reasoning engines capable of simulating both deterministic normative paths and stochastic individual trajectories.
